The UPS battery cabinet is series strings of 40 blocks. Measure each block under float. Replace any block below 13.2 volts or with an internal resistance above the string median by 30 percent. Do not mix manufacturing dates inside one string.

Align the laser shaft kit by shimming the motor feet, not by forcing the coupling. Target angular error under 0.05 degrees and offset under 0.05 millimeters. Recheck after the hold-down bolts are final-torqued.
Purge the analyzer sample line for 90 seconds before trusting a reading. The rotameter should sit on the mid mark. A low flow means a plugged filter, not a low process concentration.

Install the strain-relief on the field cable before landing conductors. Land shield drain on the chassis stud, not on the signal common. Tug-test each ferrule. Close the gland so the jacket, not the conductors, takes the pull.

Annual service on chiller CH-2 starts with a lockout of the compressor starter and a separate lockout of the crankcase heater. Recover refrigerant into a weighed cylinder and record the mass. The nameplate charge is 42 kilograms. A recovery more than 8 percent low means a leak hunt before any new charge goes in. Inspect the oil sight glass. Milky oil means moisture and requires an oil change plus a new filter-drier.

After repairs, pull a vacuum to 500 microns and hold it for 15 minutes. The rise must stay under 200 microns. Break the vacuum with the same refrigerant type, charge to the nameplate mass, and run the compressor for 20 minutes while watching superheat at the evaporator outlet. Target superheat is 6 to 8 kelvin at full load. Remove both lockouts only after the operator signs the permit.

Bridge inspection of expansion joint EJ-4 is done from the snooper truck with the right lane closed. Measure the gap at three paint marks at deck temperature, and record that temperature because the gap moves about 1 millimeter per 5 degrees. Look for torn glands, loose anchor bolts, and rust staining on the girder flange below the joint. Photograph each defect with the joint id and a scale in the frame.

Do not grind or weld from the snooper. Mark bolt holes that need replacement with paint and list them for a night closure. If the gland is torn through, cover the opening with a temporary plate screwed to the existing holes so water does not reach the bearing. The lane can reopen when the truck is clear and the temporary plate, if used, sits flush enough for a snowplow.

Retubing heat exchanger E-210 uses the U-tube bundle, not the spare straight-tube bundle stored for E-212. Match the tube alloy to the mill cert: 316L, 19.05 millimeter outside diameter, 1.65 millimeter wall. Roll the new tubes to a 5 percent wall reduction and stop. Over-rolling cracks the ligament. Hydrotest the shell side at 1.5 times design pressure for 30 minutes with the tube side open so a weep is visible.

Dry the bundle with warm air before boxing it. Cap every nozzle. Tag the crate with the exchanger id, the tube count, and the hydrotest chart number. The old bundle is drained, labeled scrap, and kept on site until the inspector releases it. Do not reuse the old gaskets. Spiral-wound replacements with the correct inner ring are in bin C-14.

Setting a radar level gauge on tank T-12 requires an empty-tank reference and a full-tank reference, or a stilling-well tape if the tank cannot move. Enter the nozzle height and the stilling-well inner diameter before the first shot. False echoes from the welds are mapped out only after the true surface echo is identified. A mapped-out true echo will read a constant level while the tank fills, which is a dangerous failure.

Compare the gauge to a manual tape at two levels at least 2 meters apart. Accept the gauge if both points fall inside 8 millimeters. Seal the housing and record the checksum of the configuration. If the checksum later changes without a work order, treat the gauge as uncalibrated and switch the tank to manual gauging until the change is explained.

Rebuilding the right-hand gearbox on crane CR-6 is a two-person job with the boom grounded in the cradle. Drain oil warm, unbolt the cover, and lift the intermediate shaft only with the threaded holes provided. Inspect gear teeth for pitting along the pitch line. Replace the pair if pitting covers more than 15 percent of a tooth face. Bearings are replaced as a set even when one looks clean, because the load history is shared.

Set backlash to the value etched inside the cover, usually 0.15 to 0.25 millimeters, using the shims under the bearing cups. Fill with the specified synthetic oil to the sight plug, not higher. Run the hoist unloaded through three full lifts and listen for a growl that tracks speed. A growl that tracks load instead of speed points at a brake, not at this gearbox. Torque the cover bolts in the printed sequence and paint-mark them.

Schema ledger keeps balanced entries. Table entry has entry_id, posted_at, source, and memo. Table line has line_id, entry_id, account, debit_cents, and credit_cents. A check on line says exactly one of debit_cents and credit_cents is positive and the other is zero. A deferred constraint trigger sums the lines of an entry and rejects the commit when the sum is not zero.

Accounts live in table account with a parent_id that must reference an account of type group. Posting accounts have type leaf and a normal_side of debit or credit. The trial balance view flips the sign according to normal_side so a credit-normal cash account does not appear as a negative asset by mistake. No view in this schema writes. Corrections are new entries that point at the original via reverses_entry_id.

The warehouse model separates location from handling unit. location has id, aisle, bay, level, and kind, where kind is reserve, forward, or dock. handling_unit has hu_id, sku, qty, and location_id, plus a status of available, held, or damaged. A partial unique index lets only one available handling unit occupy a forward location, because pick faces are single-sku.

Moves are rows in move with from_location, to_location, qty, and moved_at. The application inserts the move and updates handling_unit.location_id in one transaction. A nightly job compares the sum of available qty by sku to inventory_snapshot and writes differences to variance_log. It does not auto-adjust. A supervisor posts an adjustment entry that references the variance_log id.

Time is modeled twice on purpose. event_at is when the thing happened in the world. ingested_at is when the row landed. Both are timestamptz. Reports that say 'yesterday' filter on event_at. Freshness alerts filter on ingested_at. Mixing them made a previous dashboard show a gap that was only a late file.

Late rows are allowed. A unique key on (source, event_id) makes a replay idempotent. The loader uses insert on conflict do nothing, then counts conflicts into metric replay_drop. A conflict rate above one percent for an hour pages the owner of that source. Rows with event_at more than 40 days behind ingested_at still load, but they are flagged late so the daily aggregate job can rebuild those dates.

Permissions are rows, not columns. table principal has principal_id and kind (user or group). table grant has principal_id, action, and resource, with a unique triple. Actions are read, append, and admin. Resources are named strings such as ledger.entry or payroll.register. There is no grant that means everything. An admin grant is still one resource at a time.

Group membership is table member(group_id, user_id) with both columns pointing at principal. A check forbids a group from being a member of itself in one step. Nested groups are expanded in the effective_grant view with a depth limit of 4. The application reads only that view. Direct reads of grant are limited to the security role that edits them.

Prices are integers of minor units. price_micros is a bigint. Floating types are rejected by a column comment and by a review rule, and they do not appear in this schema. Currency is a char(3) with a foreign key to currency(code), which stores exponent so a consumer knows that JPY has exponent 0 and KWD has exponent 3.

Conversions are not stored as a column on the fact. Table fx_rate has ccy, as_of date, and usd_rate_e8, an integer scaled by 10^8. The rate is the last published rate for that date, not an average. A query that needs dollars joins the rate on currency and on the business date, and it documents the scale in the select list. Missing rates fail the query via an inner join rather than becoming a silent null.

Document store metadata sits in relational tables even though the blob lives elsewhere. table document has doc_id, sha256, byte_len, media_type, and bucket_key. table document_link attaches a document to a subject with subject_kind and subject_id, both plain text, because the subjects span several databases. A check limits subject_kind to invoice, claim, shipment, and employee.

The sha256 is unique. Uploading the same bytes twice reuses the blob and adds another link. Deleting a link does not delete the blob. A weekly job deletes blobs that have had no link for 30 days and copies their keys to purge_log first. Legal hold is a row in hold(doc_id, reason, until_on). The purge job skips any document with a hold whose until_on is null or still in the future.

If the handshake fails, move the alias back and reload again. Do not investigate while the bad chain is live. After a good handshake, revoke the old certificate at the authority and record the new serial in the change ticket.

Evacuate rack R14 before the power crew isolates the bus. Cordon every node in the rack, drain workloads with a five-minute grace, and confirm no pod still lists a node in R14. Storage volumes that are pinned to the rack must be snapshotted and reattached on R15 by the storage on-call, not by this procedure.

When the rack is empty of workloads, shut the hosts down from the BMC, not by pulling cords. Tell the power crew they may open the breaker. Stay on the bridge until they report the bus isolated. Do not power the rack back up at the end of their work. A separate change brings the nodes back one chassis at a time after facilities signs the live-bus check.

Seed the replacement search index without serving traffic from it. Create index ledger-v7 with the mapping file in the repo, set refresh_interval to -1, and start the bulk loader from the snapshot id written in the ticket. The loader is idempotent. If it stops, rerun it with the same snapshot id.

When the document count matches the snapshot count, set refresh_interval back to 1s and run the three probe queries saved under scripts/search_probes. They must return the same ids as production, ignoring score. Then add the new index to the alias as a non-serving member. Only the search owner flips the alias during the announced window. This procedure ends before that flip.

Isolate a suspected token leak. Disable the client id in the identity provider, which invalidates refresh tokens immediately. Access tokens already issued remain valid until they expire, so also block that client id at the API gateway. Rotate any downstream credential the client was allowed to read. The list is in the ticket, and it is short on purpose.

Export the last 24 hours of audit events for that client id to the incident bucket. Do not email the export. Write the disable time, the gateway rule id, and the names of the rotated credentials into the ticket. Leave the client disabled. Re-enabling it is a separate change that requires a new secret and a review of the calling service.

Hand a region to the paired site. Set the traffic dial to zero for the failing region in the global balancer and wait two minutes. Confirm request rate there has fallen to the health probes only. Drain the regional queues by stopping producers first and letting consumers finish. Do not kill consumers while a message is unacked.

When the queues are empty, scale the regional deployments to zero and snapshot their databases. Post the snapshot ids in the incident channel. The paired site is already taking writes. This procedure does not start those writers. It ends when the failing region is quiet, snapshotted, and still able to be read by the incident lead through the break-glass path.
export const quoteFee = (cents) => Math.round(cents * 1.08);
type Lane = { id: string; distanceKm: number };
export function retryAfter(attempt) { return Math.min(8000, 100 * 2 ** attempt); } The cap is eight seconds. Callers stop after attempt 6 and surface the last error rather than looping.

export function groupByVenue(fills) { const out = new Map(); for (const fill of fills) { const bucket = out.get(fill.venue) ?? []; bucket.push(fill); out.set(fill.venue, bucket); } return out; } A missing venue becomes its own bucket. The input array is not mutated.

export const isLane = (value): value is Lane => Boolean(value) && typeof value.id === 'string' && Number.isFinite(value.distanceKm); This guard is the boundary between JSON from the broker and the rest of the file. Anything else is rejected before a route is built.

export async function loadTariff(id, signal) { const res = await fetch(`/tariffs/${id}`, { signal }); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`tariff ${id} -> ${res.status}`); return res.json(); } The signal lets the screen cancel the fetch when the operator picks another tariff. There is no retry inside this function.

export function debounce(fn, waitMs) { let timer; return (...args) => { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(() => fn(...args), waitMs); }; } The search box uses a 200 ms wait. A trailing call is the only call that hits the network.

The tariff screen keeps a reducer instead of a pile of independent flags. Actions are 'load', 'ready', and 'fail'. 'load' clears the previous tariff and sets pending. 'ready' stores the payload. 'fail' stores the message and leaves the old tariff in place so the operator still sees the last good copy.

export function reduceTariff(state, action) { if (action.type === 'load') return { ...state, pending: true, error: null }; if (action.type === 'ready') return { pending: false, error: null, tariff: action.tariff }; return { ...state, pending: false, error: action.message }; } Unknown actions fall through to the fail shape only when the caller sets type 'fail'. The type union is closed, so a typo does not compile. The component reads pending to disable the save button.

Parsing a broker CSV in the browser stays off the main thread only for files above one megabyte. Smaller files run inline because worker startup cost more than the parse. The parser splits on newlines, skips a header if the first cell is lane_id, and rejects a row whose third cell is not an integer quantity.

function parseFills(text) { const rows = []; for (const line of text.split(/\n/)) { if (!line) continue; const [lane, venue, qty] = line.split(','); if (lane === 'lane_id') continue; const n = Number(qty); if (!Number.isInteger(n)) throw new Error(`bad qty ${qty}`); rows.push({ lane, venue, qty: n }); } return rows; } Quotes are not supported. The broker contract is unquoted cells. A comma inside a venue name is a file we refuse, and the error names the offending cell so the operator can send it back.

A small tokenizer class turns a filter expression into tokens for the lane search. It understands words, quoted phrases, and the operators AND and OR written in capitals.

class FilterLexer { constructor(source) { this.source = source; this.i = 0; } next() { while (this.source[this.i] === ' ') this.i += 1; const start = this.i; if (this.source[start] === '"') { this.i += 1; while (this.source[this.i] && this.source[this.i] !== '"') this.i += 1; this.i += 1; return { kind: 'phrase', text: this.source.slice(start + 1, this.i - 1) }; } while (this.source[this.i] && this.source[this.i] !== ' ') this.i += 1; const text = this.source.slice(start, this.i); if (!text) return null; if (text === 'AND' || text === 'OR') return { kind: 'op', text }; return { kind: 'word', text }; } } The lexer does not evaluate the filter. A later pass builds the boolean tree and rejects a trailing operator.
fn fee_of(cents: u32) -> u32 { cents + cents / 12 }
let lane = lanes.iter().find(|row| row.id == target);
fn clamp_u32(value: u32, cap: u32) -> u32 { if value > cap { cap } else { value } } Callers use this on a quantity that must fit a trailer. The function does not saturate a signed type.

enum Gate { Open, Held(String), Shut } fn label(gate: &Gate) -> &str { match gate { Gate::Open => "open", Gate::Held(why) => why, Gate::Shut => "shut" } } Held carries the dispatcher note. Open and Shut do not, so the UI cannot invent a reason.

fn checksum(bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 { bytes.iter().fold(0u32, |acc, b| acc.wrapping_mul(167).wrapping_add(*b as u32)) } This is a cheap fingerprint for a manifest, not a cryptographic digest. Equal fingerprints still need a full compare.

struct Ring { buf: Vec<u8>, pos: usize } impl Ring { fn push(&mut self, byte: u8) { self.buf[self.pos] = byte; self.pos = (self.pos + 1) % self.buf.len(); } } The buffer is allocated at construction and never grows. A full ring overwrites the oldest byte.

fn parse_header(line: &str) -> Option<(&str, u32)> { let mut parts = line.split(':'); let key = parts.next()?.trim(); let val: u32 = parts.next()?.trim().parse().ok()?; Some((key, val)) } A missing colon or a non-numeric value yields None. The caller logs the raw line and continues with the next header.

Tariff loading in the batch tool returns a structured error instead of a string. The miss case names the tariff id. The IO case wraps the underlying error so the log still has the path. Callers match on the enum and do not parse the display text.

enum TariffError { Missing(String), Io(std::io::Error) } fn load_tariff(path: &str) -> Result<String, TariffError> { let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(TariffError::Io)?; if text.is_empty() { return Err(TariffError::Missing(path.to_string())); } Ok(text) } The function reads the whole file. Tariffs are small. A later revision can stream, but the error type stays the same so the match arms in the driver do not change.

Lane distance is stored in meters as a newtype so a kilometer value cannot be passed by accident. The constructor rejects zero. Negative numbers cannot occur because the field is unsigned. Display divides by 1000 only at the edge, in the report printer.

struct Meters(u32); impl Meters { fn new(raw: u32) -> Option<Self> { if raw == 0 { None } else { Some(Self(raw)) } } fn get(self) -> u32 { self.0 } } Arithmetic that would mix meters and millimeters has no implementation, which is the point. The report printer is the only place that formats a unit suffix, and it receives Meters rather than a bare integer.

A worker thread owns the socket and sends parsed fills to the UI thread over a channel. The worker shuts down when the channel closes, which happens when the UI drops the receiver. There is no shared mutable buffer.

fn pump(rx_stop: std::sync::mpsc::Receiver<()>, tx: std::sync::mpsc::Sender<String>) { loop { if rx_stop.try_recv().is_ok() { break; } let _ = tx.send(String::from("tick")); } } The real reader replaces the tick with a line from the socket. The shape of the shutdown is what this sketch fixes: the worker does not need a flag behind a mutex, and dropping the UI side is enough to end it.
func HarborToll(gross int) int { return gross - gross/12 }
if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("lane %s: %w", id, err) }
func ClampInt(value, cap int) int { if value > cap { return cap }; return value } The payments service uses this before writing a trailer quantity. It does not treat a negative cap as a special case.

type Lane struct { ID string; Km int } func FindLane(lanes []Lane, id string) (Lane, bool) { for _, lane := range lanes { if lane.ID == id { return lane, true } }; return Lane{}, false } The boolean is false when the id is absent. Callers must not read the zero Lane in that case.

func RetryWait(attempt int) time.Duration { wait := time.Duration(100*(1<<attempt)) * time.Millisecond; if wait > 8*time.Second { return 8 * time.Second }; return wait } Attempt 0 waits 100 milliseconds. The shift stops being useful past attempt 6, which is also where the caller gives up.

func GroupByVenue(fills []Fill) map[string][]Fill { out := map[string][]Fill{}; for _, fill := range fills { out[fill.Venue] = append(out[fill.Venue], fill) }; return out } A nil input yields an empty map, not a nil map, so a later range is safe. The function does not sort the groups.

func ParseQty(raw string) (int, error) { n, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(raw)); if err != nil { return 0, fmt.Errorf("qty %q: %w", raw, err) }; if n < 0 { return 0, fmt.Errorf("qty %d is negative", n) }; return n, nil } Empty strings fail the integer parse. The error includes the original text so the bad cell can be found in the file.

The tariff loader reads a small JSON file and decodes it into a struct with explicit fields. Unknown fields are an error. A silent drop hid a renamed key for a week last year, so DisallowUnknownFields stays on. The file is closed with defer before the decode error is returned.

func LoadTariff(path string) (Tariff, error) { f, err := os.Open(path); if err != nil { return Tariff{}, err }; defer f.Close(); dec := json.NewDecoder(f); dec.DisallowUnknownFields(); var t Tariff; if err := dec.Decode(&t); err != nil { return Tariff{}, err }; return t, nil } Tariff contains ID, Currency, and PerKm cents. The decoder does not call any method on Tariff. Validation of a zero PerKm happens in the caller, next to the business rule that names the minimum.

HTTP handlers in this service return early on a bad quantity and write a short plain-text body. They do not render HTML. The status is 400 for a bad quantity and 404 when the lane id is unknown. Logging happens at the middleware, so the handler only builds the message.

func QtyHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { n, err := ParseQty(r.URL.Query().Get("n")); if err != nil { http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest); return }; fmt.Fprintf(w, "%d\n", n) } The query key is n. A missing key parses as an empty string and fails in ParseQty, which is the same path as a non-numeric value. The handler does not look at the request body.

Worker shutdown listens on a context and on the job channel together. When the context is canceled, the worker returns even if jobs remain. The caller decides whether to requeue those jobs. A nil job is ignored so a closed-channel zero value cannot be processed by mistake.

func Run(ctx context.Context, jobs <-chan Job) { for { select { case <-ctx.Done(): return; case job, ok := <-jobs: if !ok { return }; if job.ID == "" { continue }; job.Do() } } } Job.Do is synchronous. The worker does not start another goroutine per job, which keeps the shutdown story to this single loop. Tests cancel the context and assert that Do was not called for a job sent afterward.
long wharfage(long crates) { return crates * 3 + 40; }
record Lane(String id, int km) {}
int capPick(int asked, int tote) { return asked > tote ? tote : asked; } The trailer screen calls this with a positive cap. A negative value passes through unchanged.

Optional<Lane> findLane(List<Lane> lanes, String id) { return lanes.stream().filter(row -> row.id().equals(id)).findFirst(); } An empty Optional means the id is unknown. Callers branch before reading the lane.

Duration retryWait(int attempt) { long ms = 100L << attempt; return Duration.ofMillis(Math.min(ms, 8000)); } The shift is done on a long so attempt 6 does not overflow an int. The cap is eight seconds.

Map<String, List<Fill>> groupByVenue(List<Fill> fills) { return fills.stream().collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Fill::venue)); } The map is mutable. A later step sorts each list by timestamp without rebuilding the grouping.

int parseQty(String raw) { int n = Integer.parseInt(raw.trim()); if (n < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("negative qty"); return n; } NumberFormatException still propagates for a blank cell. The negative check is the only extra rule.

Tariff files are read with a buffered reader and a single JSON library call. The method throws a checked IOException to the batch driver, which already knows how to mark a file as failed and move on. It does not catch a parse error and turn it into an empty tariff.

Tariff loadTariff(Path path) throws IOException { try (Reader reader = Files.newBufferedReader(path)) { return JSON.std.beanFrom(Tariff.class, reader); } } Tariff is a plain class with public fields id, currency, and perKm. The binder fails if perKm is missing. That failure is what we want, because a default of zero would undercharge a lane.

The quantity endpoint reads one query parameter and writes a plain integer. There is no session and no template. A bad integer becomes status 400 with the exception message as the body. The method is deliberately small so the filter chain can be tested without it.

void qty(HttpExchange ex) throws IOException { String raw = ex.getRequestURI().getQuery(); int n; try { n = parseQty(raw.substring(2)); } catch (RuntimeException err) { byte[] msg = err.getMessage().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8); ex.sendResponseHeaders(400, msg.length); ex.getResponseBody().write(msg); return; } byte[] body = (n + "\n").getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8); ex.sendResponseHeaders(200, body.length); ex.getResponseBody().write(body); } The query is expected to look like n=12. A missing equals sign throws and becomes a 400 as well. The exchange is closed by the server wrapper, not by this method.

A scheduled job pulls lane closures from a queue and writes them to a journal file. The lock is a file lock so two hosts cannot append the same journal. If the lock is busy, the job skips this minute and tries again on the next tick.

void drain(Queue<String> closures, Path journal) throws IOException { try (FileChannel ch = FileChannel.open(journal, StandardOpenOption.APPEND, StandardOpenOption.CREATE)) { FileLock lock = ch.tryLock(); if (lock == null) return; for (String line : closures) { ch.write(ByteBuffer.wrap((line + "\n").getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))); } } } tryLock does not wait. The queue is left intact when the lock is busy, because the items are only removed by the caller after a true return. The journal is line oriented and is safe to tail from another process.
int fee_of(int cents) { return cents + cents / 12; }
auto open_lanes = std::vector<int>{}; open_lanes.reserve(64);
int clamp_int(int value, int cap) { return value > cap ? cap : value; } Used when a pick quantity must fit one tote. The function is header-only and has no state.

std::optional<Lane> find_lane(const std::vector<Lane>& lanes, std::string_view id) { for (const auto& lane : lanes) if (lane.id == id) return lane; return std::nullopt; } nullopt is not a default lane. The caller prints a miss and keeps the previous selection.

std::chrono::milliseconds retry_wait(int attempt) { auto ms = 100 * (1 << attempt); return std::chrono::milliseconds(ms > 8000 ? 8000 : ms); } Attempt is assumed small. The shift is not guarded against a negative attempt, which the caller never produces.

uint32_t checksum(std::span<const uint8_t> bytes) { uint32_t acc = 0; for (auto b : bytes) acc = acc * 167u + b; return acc; } This fingerprint tags a manifest in logs. It is not a substitute for comparing the bytes when a match matters.

struct Ring { std::vector<uint8_t> buf; size_t pos{}; void push(uint8_t byte) { buf[pos] = byte; pos = (pos + 1) % buf.size(); } }; The vector is sized once by the constructor that is not shown here. push never allocates.

The manifest reader owns a file descriptor and yields one record at a time. A short read at end of file returns an empty optional. Any other short read throws. The buffer is a member so the hot path does not allocate.

class Reader { int fd; std::string buf; public: explicit Reader(int f) : fd(f) {} std::optional<std::string> next() { buf.clear(); char ch; while (true) { auto n = ::read(fd, &ch, 1); if (n == 0) return buf.empty() ? std::nullopt : std::optional<std::string>(buf); if (ch == '\n') return buf; buf.push_back(ch); } } }; Reading one byte at a time is acceptable because manifests are read once at startup. The caller closes the descriptor. Reader does not, so a stack instance cannot surprise a surrounding scope.

Distances inside the planner are millimeters held in a strong typedef, implemented as an enum class with an explicit constructor. Adding two distances is allowed. Adding a distance to a raw integer is not, which caught a unit bug in review of the first port.

enum class Mm : int {}; constexpr Mm operator+(Mm a, Mm b) { return Mm{static_cast<int>(a) + static_cast<int>(b)}; } The cast is confined to this operator. Call sites read like ordinary addition. A formatter in the report tool divides by 1000 when it prints meters, and that division is the only one in the program.

The socket thread pushes complete lines into a mutex-protected deque and notifies a condition variable. The UI thread waits with a timeout so a stuck socket cannot freeze the window forever. A shutdown flag is checked on both sides.

void push_line(std::deque<std::string>& q, std::mutex& mu, std::condition_variable& cv, std::string line) { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mu); q.push_back(std::move(line)); cv.notify_one(); } pop_line is the matching wait and is not shown. It returns false when the shutdown flag is set, even if the deque still holds lines. Those leftover lines are discarded on purpose during exit.
decimal Stamp(decimal basis) => basis * 0.04m;
var lane = lanes.First(row => row.Id == target);
int LimitPick(int asked, int tote) => asked > tote ? tote : asked; The tote planner calls this with a cap taken from the box record. A larger pick is cut down, not rejected.

Lane? FindLane(IEnumerable<Lane> lanes, string id) => lanes.FirstOrDefault(row => row.Id == id); Null means the id is absent. The method does not throw for a miss, because misses are common during typing.

TimeSpan RetryWait(int attempt) { var ms = Math.Min(8000, 100 * (1 << attempt)); return TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(ms); } The shift uses an int and is safe through attempt 6, which is the last attempt the caller will make.

Dictionary<string, List<Fill>> GroupByVenue(IEnumerable<Fill> fills) => fills.GroupBy(f => f.Venue).ToDictionary(g => g.Key, g => g.ToList()); Each list is a fresh list. Sorting one group later does not reorder the original sequence.

int ParseQty(string raw) { var n = int.Parse(raw.Trim(), CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); if (n < 0) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(raw)); return n; } Invariant culture avoids a comma being read as a thousands separator on a workstation set to another locale.

Tariff JSON is deserialized with a source generator so the batch job does not pay for reflection at startup. Property names match the file. A missing perKm property throws, and the job moves that file to the reject folder with the exception text beside it.

Tariff LoadTariff(string path) { var json = File.ReadAllText(path); return JsonSerializer.Deserialize(json, TariffJsonContext.Default.Tariff) ?? throw new InvalidDataException(path); } The null check covers a file that is the token null. An empty object fails earlier because perKm is required. The context class is generated and is not written by hand.

The minimal API for quantity parses the query and writes a bare integer. There is no view engine. Model binding is skipped on purpose so a non-integer cannot become zero. The lambda is the whole endpoint.

app.MapGet("/qty", (string n) => { var value = ParseQty(n); return Results.Text(value.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)); }); A missing n is rejected by the framework before the lambda runs. ParseQty still guards a negative value. The response is text, not JSON, because the consumer is a shell script on the dock PC.

Channel writes from the socket reader are bounded. When the channel is full, the reader waits. It does not drop a line. The UI consumes on a timer and posts back to the dispatcher thread, so a burst of lines cannot touch a widget directly.

var channel = Channel.CreateBounded<string>(new BoundedChannelOptions(256) { FullMode = BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait }); The capacity 256 is about four seconds of the busiest feed we have measured. A wait that lasts longer than that shows up as a stalled socket in the existing metrics, which is the signal we already page on.
select lane_id, sum(qty) from fill where venue = 'XLON' group by lane_id;
create index ix_fill_venue on fill (venue, ts) where qty > 0;

select buyer_id, count(*) as open_n from invoice where balance_cents > 0 group by buyer_id having count(*) > 3; Buyers with three or fewer open invoices are omitted. The screen pages from this result, not from the base table.
update lane set status = 'held' where id = :id and status = 'open'; The status predicate makes the update a no-op if another session already held the lane. The application checks the row count.

select e.entry_id, sum(l.debit_cents) - sum(l.credit_cents) as net from entry e join line l using (entry_id) group by e.entry_id having sum(l.debit_cents) <> sum(l.credit_cents); This hunt should return no rows. A row here means a broken entry that the deferred trigger failed to stop.
delete from session_token where expires_at < now() - interval '2 days'; The two-day cushion keeps a token that expired during a long weekend available for the audit query. Older rows are gone.

insert into fx_rate (ccy, as_of, usd_rate_e8) values (:ccy, :as_of, :rate) on conflict (ccy, as_of) do update set usd_rate_e8 = excluded.usd_rate_e8; A republished rate for the same day replaces the stored one. There is no history table for this feed.

The open-invoice report joins buyer once and aggregates in the database. Pulling every invoice into the app and summing there was slower and drifted whenever a new status was added. The query below is the one the report runs.

select b.name, count(i.invoice_id) as n, sum(i.balance_cents) as cents from buyer b join invoice i on i.buyer_id = b.buyer_id where i.balance_cents > 0 and i.due_on < current_date group by b.name order by cents desc; Due dates in the future are excluded, so the report is a past-due list and not a full receivables list. Name collisions across buyers would merge their totals, and buyer.name is unique for that reason.

Replay of a fill file uses a staging table and a single insert that skips rows already present. The natural key is source file plus line number. A second load of the same file adds nothing and reports the conflict count.

insert into fill (source, line_no, lane_id, qty) select s.source, s.line_no, s.lane_id, s.qty from fill_stage s on conflict (source, line_no) do nothing; The statement returns the number of inserted rows through the driver, and the loader subtracts that from the stage count to get skips. Staging is truncated after a successful insert, including when every row was a skip.

A window function numbers fills inside a lane so the desk can see the sequence without a self join. The ordering is the exchange timestamp, and a tie breaks on the fill id so the numbers are stable across reruns.

select lane_id, fill_id, qty, row_number() over (partition by lane_id order by ts, fill_id) as seq from fill where ts >= :start and ts < :end; The end bound is exclusive so adjacent windows do not double-count a fill that lands on the boundary. The desk exports this result. It is not stored. A stored sequence went stale the first time a late fill arrived.
rsync -a --delete /var/snap/ledger/ /backup/ledger/
journalctl -u payments-api --since '1 hour ago' -p err
find /var/log/ledger -name '*.gz' -mtime +30 -delete Compressed logs older than 30 days are removed. The live file is not compressed and is not matched by this name.
tar -C /var/lib -czf /backup/tariff-$(date +%F).tgz tariff The archive is rooted at tariff/, not at /var/lib, so a restore can unpack it in a scratch directory.
ss -lptn 'sport = :8080' The operator runs this before a restart to see which process still holds the port. An empty answer means the port is free.
awk -F, 'NR>1 { qty[$1]+=$3 } END { for (k in qty) print k, qty[k] }' fills.csv Field one is the lane and field three is the quantity. The header is skipped. The order of the print is not sorted.

curl -fsS --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 -o tariff.json https://files.internal/tariff/current.json A failed retry leaves no partial file because curl writes to a temporary name and the -o file appears only on success.

The night backup script refuses to run if the previous archive is missing or tiny. A zero-byte file from a full disk once replaced a good archive, so size is checked before the new run deletes anything. The script logs to stdout and lets the timer capture it.

#!/bin/sh set -eu prev=/backup/ledger-prev.tgz test -s "$prev" tar -C /var/lib -czf /backup/ledger-new.tgz ledger mv /backup/ledger-new.tgz "$prev" set -eu aborts on a failed test or a failed tar. The mv happens only after tar returns success, so a failed tar leaves the previous archive in place. There is no deletion of the source tree.

A deploy helper reads a tag, checks that the working tree is clean, and checks out that tag in a detached state. It does not pull. The remote update is a separate command the operator already ran. A dirty tree stops the helper before any checkout.

#!/bin/sh set -eu tag=$1 git diff --quiet git checkout --detach "$tag" The quiet diff exits non-zero when tracked files differ. Untracked files are ignored by that check, and the operator is expected to notice them. The helper takes the tag as its only argument and does not invent a default.

Log shipping uses a lock directory so two overlapping timers cannot upload the same hour twice. mkdir is the lock. It is atomic on one filesystem. A stale lock older than two hours is removed, because a crashed shipper should not block the rest of the day.

#!/bin/sh set -eu lock=/var/lock/ship-ledger if ! mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; then find "$lock" -mmin +120 -exec rmdir {} \;; mkdir "$lock"; fi After the upload, the script removes the lock. A failure mid-upload leaves the lock, and the next run waits until the two-hour rule clears it. That delay is acceptable. A double upload was not.
fee = ->(cents) { cents + cents / 12 }
picked = roster.detect { |item| item.sku == wanted }
clamp = ->(value, cap) { value > cap ? cap : value } The picker calls this with integers. It is a lambda, not a method on a class, so there is no receiver to misuse.
grouped = fills.group_by { |fill| fill.venue } The hash values are arrays in input order. A venue that never appears is simply absent, not mapped to an empty array.
wait = ->(attempt) { [8000, 100 * (2**attempt)].min } The result is milliseconds. The caller sleeps with that number divided by 1000.0 only at the edge.
qty = raw.strip.to_i to_i turns a blank string into 0, which is the wrong failure mode, so the caller rejects a string that does not match a digits-only pattern before this line.

checksum = bytes.each_with_object(0) { |b, acc| (acc * 167 + b) & 0xffffffff } The mask keeps the accumulator inside 32 bits. This tags a manifest in a log line and is not used for integrity against a malicious file.

Tariff loading uses the standard JSON library and a plain hash. There is no schema gem. Required keys are checked with fetch, which raises KeyError and names the key. That exception is enough for the batch driver to reject the file.

A ring buffer keeps the last 64 log lines for the status page. It is an array plus an index. When it fills, the next write overwrites the oldest line. The page reads a copy so a concurrent push cannot change the array while it is being joined.

ring = Array.new(64) pos = 0 push_line = lambda do |line| ring[pos] = line pos = (pos + 1) % ring.length end snapshot = lambda { ring.compact } compact drops the nil slots that exist before the ring has wrapped once. After that, the snapshot has 64 lines and the oldest is the one just after pos.

El rotulo del horno declara 42 kW y un factor de potencia de 0.92. La corriente de linea calculada en 400 V queda cerca de 68 amperios. El interruptor de 80 amperios tiene margen.
El horno de solera usa tres zonas con consignas independientes. Zona 1 en 180 grados, zona 2 en 210, zona 3 en 190. El ventilador de recirculacion no arranca si una puerta queda abierta.
La resistencia de techo del horno mide 18 ohm en frio. En caliente sube. Una lectura bajo 12 ohm en frio indica una espira en cortocircuito y se cambia el elemento.
El variador del ventilador del horno es de 4 kW y lleva filtro de entrada. El cable de potencia y el de señal van por bandejas distintas para no inducir ruido en la termocupla.
La parada de emergencia del horno corta contactores de potencia y deja el circuito de mando con 24 V. Rearmar exige girar el hongo y pulsar el rearme en el tablero, no solo cerrar la puerta.
El horno nuevo pide puesta de tierra menor de 1 ohm y un diferencial de 300 mA en la acometida. La medicion de esta mañana fue 0.4 ohm. El diferencial de prueba disparó en 180 ms.
La rampa de arranque del horno limita la corriente al 40 por ciento durante 30 segundos. Sin esa rampa el pico supera el ajuste del interruptor y la linea de la nave se cae.
El registro del horno guarda temperatura de zona y estado del contactor cada minuto. Un hueco de más de cinco minutos se marca como falla de adquisicion, no como enfriamiento real.

La puerta del horno tiene un fin de carrera en serie con el contactor de resistencias. Si el fin de carrera falla cerrado, el enclavamiento no ve la puerta abierta y eso es un defecto que impide producir.
El ensayo de aislacion del horno se hace con 500 V en corriente continua con las resistencias desconectadas del variador. El minimo aceptado es 1 megaohm. Hoy dio 8.

El tablero del horno de cinta está dividido en celda de potencia y celda de mando. La celda de potencia lleva los contactores de 42 kW y las protecciones. La de mando lleva el PLC y las fuentes de 24 V. Un operador no abre la celda de potencia: eso queda para el electricista con el bloqueo puesto. La consignacion de temperatura se cambia desde la pantalla sin abrir ninguna celda.

Ayer la zona 2 no alcanzaba la consigna. El contactor cerraba y la corriente de esa zona era cero. La resistencia estaba abierta. Se cambió el elemento en la parada de la tarde y la corriente quedó en 32 amperios, que es lo esperado para esa zona. El registro de la falla queda con la hora de la alarma y la hora del recambio.

La especificación eléctrica del horno pide alimentación 400 V más o menos 5 por ciento y frecuencia 50 Hz. La planta midió 389 V en el horario pico y 408 V de madrugada. Ambos valores entran. Si el pico baja de 380 V el horno debe alarmar y no seguir con las resistencias, porque el tiempo de ciclo se alarga y el producto sale fuera de curva. Esa alarma hoy está en aviso, no en corte, y el jefe de mantenimiento quiere pasarla al modo corte.

El cambio no es de parametro de cocción: es de protección. Se documenta en el plano unifilar y en la lista de alarmas. El fabricante confirma por escrito que cortar resistencias ante subtension no daña el ventilador, que sigue en marcha para no dejar calor estancado.

El horno de laboratorio, de 6 kW, no comparte tablero con el de producción. Tiene su propio diferencial de 30 mA porque hay personal al lado durante el ensayo. La termocupla es de vaina expuesta y el controlador es un PID con salida por rele, no por tiristor. La consigna de calibración es 150 grados y la tolerancia del informe es más o menos 2.

El ultimo contraste contra el patron dio 149.2 grados. Se dejó el offset del controlador en cero. Si el proximo contraste se va más de 2 grados se ajusta el offset y se anota en la ficha del instrumento, no en la del horno de produccion. Son equipos distintos y mezclar sus fichas ya causó un error de escala el año pasado.

El cálculo de cable del horno usa la corriente de 68 amperios y un tendido de 40 metros en bandeja perforada. La seccion elegida es 25 milimetros cuadrados de cobre, que admite esa corriente segun el coeficiente de bandeja. La caida de tension calculada es 1.6 por ciento, bajo el 3 por ciento que pide el pliego. El neutro no se usa: la carga es equilibrada en estrella sin neutro.

La puesta de tierra viaja en un conductor aparte de 16 milimetros cuadrados, no en la armadura del cable. El proyecto lo dice asi porque la bandeja no es continua en el tramo del techo. El electricista midió continuidad de tierra antes de energizar y anotó 0.3 ohm desde el horno hasta la barra principal.

La secuencia de encendido del horno es fija. Primero el extractor, después el ventilador de recirculacion, y solo entonces las resistencias. Si el extractor no confirma marcha en 10 segundos, las resistencias no entran. Esa condicion evita acumular vapor y calor con el ducto cerrado. El PLC lo implementa con un temporizador, no con un retardo del operador.

En la prueba del sabado se abrió el extractor y se inhibió su confirmación. Las resistencias no entraron y la alarma salió en la pantalla. Luego se restituyó la confirmación y la secuencia completó. La prueba queda firmada en el protocolo de puesta en marcha. No se repite en cada arranque diario: el enclavamiento ya queda activo.

El horno consume en vacio 9 kW, casi todo del ventilador y del extractor. Con carga y consigna estable el promedio de una hora fue 27 kW, no los 42 de placa. La placa es la potencia instalada, no el consumo medio. Usar 42 para estimar la factura electrica sobra un tercio y distorsiona el costo del turno.

El medidor de la acometida del horno registra energia activa y no reactiva, porque el variador ya compensa. El informe semanal muestra kWh por hora de puerta cerrada y kWh por hora de puerta abierta. La hora de puerta abierta cuesta casi el doble. Por eso el procedimiento pide agrupar las cargas y no abrir la puerta en cada bandeja.
Humedad del grano en cosecha: 18.4 por ciento en el lote norte.
Rendimiento de cosecha del lote norte: 6.2 toneladas por hectarea.
El silo 4 recibe la cosecha y la seca hasta 14 por ciento de humedad.
Durante la cosecha el viento fue del este y no hubo lluvia en seis horas.
La cosecha de trigo del lote 12 empezó con 16 por ciento de humedad y terminó en 14. El secado en planta no hizo falta. El grano fue directo al silo 2.
La cosechadora dejó una franja sin cortar junto al alambrado por un nido marcado. Esa franja se estimó en 0.3 hectareas y no entra en el rendimiento del lote.
El flete de la cosecha hasta el acopio cuesta 18 por tonelada en los primeros 30 km. Pasado ese radio suma 0.4 por kilometro. El lote sur cae dentro del radio.
La tolva de la cosechadora se descarga en menos de tres minutos si el carretón está nivelado. Con desnivel el sinfin corta por torque y hay que reubicar el equipo.
El parte de cosecha anota hectareas, humedad, peso de balanza y descuento por impurezas. Hoy el descuento fue 1.1 por ciento, bajo el 2 que acepta el acopio sin recargo.
Antes de la cosecha se calibró el monitor de rendimiento con una pasada de 200 metros pesada en la balanza del campo. El error quedó en 2 por ciento. No se tocó de nuevo el factor.
La lluvia de 12 mm del martes detuvo la cosecha medio día. El suelo del lote bajo no aguantó el carro. Se siguió solo en la loma, con humedad de grano todavía en 17.
El secador continuo de la planta toma la cosecha húmeda y la entrega en 14 por ciento. El consumo de gas de ayer fue 1.3 litros equivalentes por punto de humedad y por tonelada.
La impureza del lote 7, medida en el acopio, fue 3.4 por ciento por grano verde. Se decidió esperar cuatro días de cosecha en ese lote para no pagar el descuento mayor.
El seguro de granizo cubre la cosecha en pie hasta el momento del corte, no el grano ya en el silo. El parte del inspector estimó 20 por ciento de daño en el lote oeste y ninguno en el este.

El plan de cosecha de la semana ordena los lotes por humedad y por piso, no por cercania al camino. El lote 4 está en 19 por ciento y con piso firme: entra primero al secador. El lote 9 está en 15 y puede esperar en planta sin secado, pero el piso no aguanta el carro después de las 16 horas. Por eso el 9 se corta de mañana temprano y el 4 ocupa el secador de tarde.

La cosechadora es una sola. Cambiar de lote cuesta cuarenta minutos de traslado. Ese tiempo está cargado en el plan y no se esconde en el rendimiento. Si llueve el jueves, el 4 se prioriza igual porque cada día por encima de 18 por ciento suma descuento en el acopio.

La balanza de la cooperativa descuenta impureza y humedad sobre el peso bruto de cada carta de porte de la cosecha. Un camión de 28 toneladas con 17 por ciento de humedad y 1 por ciento de impureza no acredita 28 toneladas en la cuenta del productor. La formula está impresa detrás de la carta. El encargado del campo la revisa antes de firmar, porque un punto de humedad mal cargado cambia el saldo.

Ayer un camión salió con 16.5 en el medidor del campo y el acopio midió 17.2. La diferencia cabe en la tolerancia de 1 punto que el contrato acepta sin arbitraje. No se abrió reclamo. Se anotó el par de valores para ver si el medidor del campo se corre en los proximos tres camiones.

El rendimiento informado por el monitor de la cosechadora no reemplaza la balanza. Sirve para ver franjas dentro del lote: la cabecera dio 4.8 toneladas por hectarea y el centro 6.4. Esa diferencia coincide con el mapa de suelo, no con una falla del cabezal. El total del monitor, 92 toneladas, se compara con la suma de las cartas de porte al cerrar el lote.

Al cierre las cartas sumaron 89 toneladas. La brecha de 3 toneladas es 3 por ciento, arriba del 2 que se tolera para dar por bueno el monitor. Se recalibra antes del proximo lote. No se corrige el mapa ya exportado: se archiva con la nota de la brecha.

Guardar la cosecha en silo bolsa exige humedad bajo 14 por ciento y un piso que no junte agua. El lote embolsado el lunes estaba en 13.6 y el piso es una loma. Se midió la bolsa al tercer día: 13.8, sin olor de fermento. Una subida sobre 15 exigiria extraer y secar, con merma y con flete doble.

La bolsa no es el destino final. El contrato de venta de mayo pide entrega en el acopio. Hasta entonces el grano sigue siendo del productor y el seguro de silo bolsa, no el de granizo, es el que aplica. El parte semanal incluye metros de bolsa, humedad y la fecha prevista de extracción.

El personal de cosecha rota en turnos de diez horas con una hora de solape para pasar el parte. En el solape se informan atascos, humedad y cualquier mezcla de cultivares, que el acopio paga distinto. No se mezcla el cultivar corto con el largo en la misma tolva. Una mezcla fuerza la venta del camión como condición cámara y baja el precio.

El martes el turno mañana cortó el cultivar largo hasta el alambrado medio y dejó el corto para la tarde. El parte lo dice y las cartas de porte coinciden. No hubo mezcla. El precio del largo se mantuvo. El corto, con mas proteina, se vendió en el contrato separado que ya estaba abierto.

Cerrar la cosecha del establecimiento pide tres numeros que tienen que coincidir: hectareas de los lotes, toneladas de las cartas y el remanente en planta. Si la suma de cartas más el remanente no explica el rendimiento por hectarea, hay grano sin carta o una carta duplicada. Este año las 640 hectareas dieron 3520 toneladas en cartas y 80 en el silo propio. El rendimiento medio es 5.6 toneladas por hectarea, alineado con el monitor despues de la recalibracion.

Queda abierta solo la bolsa del lote 3, con 40 toneladas ya incluidas en las 80. No hay camion sin carta. El seguro de granizo se cierra con el acta de fin de cosecha, que el inspector firma cuando no queda cultivo en pie. Esa acta no incluye el grano embolsado: ese riesgo ya pasó al seguro de almacen.
